newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium ends lower on first volatile day.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium ends lower on first volatile day.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures ended their first trading day sharply lower on Monday, with two contracts hitting the daily six yen limit-down, on speculative sales from local traders and individual investors, traders said.
The October and the December contract fell by six yen in the afternoon to 205.4 yen and 204.0 yen per kg, respectively, but recovered by the close.
The benchmark February 1998 contract closed at 205.1 yen, down from 210.3 at the opening. The daily volume was estimated at 19,645 lots.

"Frankly speaking, we're not sure what caused the price plunge today. But some local traders and individual investors generated active speculative selling particularly in the afternoon session," a brokerage house trader said.
The aluminium contract at the Tokyo Commodity Exchange is the first base metal futures contract ever traded in Japan.
Asian metal traders expect three month London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices to shed between $10-$20 a tonne later today, with the market under selling pressure.
But most saw strong support around the $2,300 a tonne level. Three-month copper was indicated at $2,327/$2,332 at 1900 GMT on Friday.
The traders said three month LME aluminium should be able to withstand current selling pressure.
Three-month aluminium was indicated at $1,623/$1,625 during late trade in London on Friday.
